bugs.title: Magnet metadata fetch stalls forever at a fixed byte count with one connected peer that never progresses — DHT and peer exchange are not enabled for the metadata-only aria2 invocation
bugs.notes: Seeded from sweep prompt. Metadata-only aria2c invocation in pipeline/stage_a/ingest.py (~line 974, logs 'Fetching magnet metadata via aria2 (metadata-only, bounded)') lacks --enable-dht=true / --enable-dht6=true / --enable-peer-exchange=true, unlike _download_torrent_payload() which sets DHT+PEX. Observed failure: CN:1, byte count frozen at 395KiB(0%) for the entire run until --bt-stop-timeout=120 killed it. Fix: add DHT/DHT6/PEX flags to the metadata-only invocation; consider DHT bootstrap warm-up, supplementary --bt-tracker (additive only), and whether 120s stop-timeout is still right. Must NOT reintroduce exit-code-based success check (bug-04 comment at lines 975-981 stays). Verify empirically against a live well-seeded magnet if internet allows; be honest in notes about what was tested. Add a bug-64 note after the existing bug-04 comment block without altering it. | DONE (commit 26fa18c): Added --enable-dht=true --enable-dht6=true --enable-peer-exchange=true to the metadata-only aria2c invocation in _resolve_magnet_metadata(), plus a supplemental --bt-tracker list mirroring _download_torrent_payload(). EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED in this sandbox (aria2 1.37.0, fresh env, no prior DHT state): (1) OLD flags vs a tracker-less live Sintel magnet stalled at CN:0 for the full 60s stop-timeout, no metadata saved; (2) NEW flags found CN:29 via DHT within ~15s and saved the 20KB .torrent in ~23s -- proves DHT bootstrap works out of the box in a clean CI-like env, so no --dht-file-path warm-up file was added. (3) --bt-tracker merge semantics verified empirically: a dummy torrent with an embedded tracker run with a flag tracker showed BOTH announce URLs active in aria2's debug log -- additive, never replaces embedded trackers, matching the man page ('additional tracker'). --bt-stop-timeout raised 120->180s (not more): DHT warm-up needs a little longer than a pure tracker hit, but 180s plus the existing outer timeout-600/subprocess-620 keeps worst-case dead-swarm latency bounded. Deliberately did NOT touch: the bug-04 comment block (appended after it instead), the check=False invocation, or the saved-metadata-file success check. Sanity: python ast.parse on ingest.py passes.
